issues.t: Ignition switch can slip out of Run (recall)
issues.sym: The engine suddenly shuts off while driving, often after hitting a bump or bumping the key ring with your knee. Steering and braking get much heavier.
issues.why: The ignition switch was made with too little turning resistance, so a heavy key ring or a jolt can move it from Run to Accessory. That cuts the engine and can keep the airbags from deploying in a crash. This defect was linked to deaths, and GM recall 14V-047 replaces the switch.
issues.next: Check your VIN right away for open recall 14V-047. Until it's fixed, use only the ignition key with nothing else on the ring.

issues.sym: The steering suddenly becomes very heavy, especially at low speed, and a power steering warning may show. It can come and go.
issues.why: The electric power steering motor or its sensor fails, so the system stops helping you steer. GM recalls 10V-073 and 14V-153 replace the motor, and GM extended coverage on it.
issues.next: Hold the wheel firmly and slow down; you can still steer, it just takes more effort. Check your VIN for open recalls 10V-073 and 14V-153.

issues.t: Key can come out when not in Off (recall)
issues.sym: You can pull the key out of the ignition even though it isn't fully in the Off position.
issues.why: Wear in the ignition lock cylinder lets the key come out early. With an automatic, the car might not be in Park and could roll away. GM recall 14V-171 replaces the lock cylinder.
issues.next: Always set the parking brake. Check your VIN for open recall 14V-171.

issues.t: Key gets stuck in the ignition
issues.sym: The key won't turn back to Off or won't come out, even with the shifter in Park.
issues.why: On automatic cars the shifter has to tell the ignition it's in Park before the key will release. A worn shifter switch, cable or lock cylinder breaks that link.
issues.next: Jiggle the shifter firmly in Park and try again. A shop can test the shifter's park switch and cable; the shifter or lock cylinder is the usual fix.

issues.t: Fuel pump module can crack and leak gas (recall)
issues.sym: A gasoline smell inside or around the car, sometimes with fuel dripping under the rear seat area.
issues.why: Plastic ports on the fuel pump module on top of the tank can crack and leak fuel, which is a fire risk. GM recalls 09V-419 and 12V-459 replace or repair the module.
issues.next: If you smell gas, don't drive it or park it in a garage. Check your VIN for open recalls 09V-419 and 12V-459.

issues.t: Timing chain rattle and tensioner failure
issues.sym: A rattle from the engine on cold starts, a check engine light for timing codes, rough running, or in the worst case the engine won't start.
issues.why: The timing chain tensioner and guides wear, especially if the oil runs low or isn't changed often, and the chain stretches and slaps.
issues.next: Keep the oil full and changed on schedule. If the rattle lasts or timing codes appear, have the chain, guides and tensioner replaced before the chain jumps and damages the engine.

issues.sym: The engine shakes or stumbles, especially when accelerating, the check engine light flashes, and the car may lose power or even stall.
issues.why: The ignition coil pack (ignition module) fails, so one or more cylinders stop firing.
issues.next: A flashing check engine light means stop driving hard, because unburned fuel can ruin the catalytic converter. Have the codes read; the coil pack and spark plugs are usually replaced together.

issues.t: Check gas cap message and check engine light
issues.sym: A Check Gas Cap message or check engine light, sometimes with a slight fuel smell near the filler.
issues.why: A worn gas cap seal or a corroded fuel filler neck lets fuel vapor escape, and the emissions system flags a leak.
issues.next: Tighten the cap until it clicks. If the message returns, try a new cap; if that doesn't fix it, have the filler neck and evaporative system smoke-tested.

issues.t: Front lower control arm bushings wear out
issues.sym: A clunk or knock from the front over bumps, a shimmy or vibration at speed, or the car pulling and wearing tires unevenly.
issues.why: The rubber bushings in the front lower control arms crack and wear, letting the arm move around.
issues.next: Have the front end inspected. The usual fix is new control arms with fresh bushings, followed by an alignment.

issues.sym: Grinding when shifting into some gears, often 2nd or 3rd, or gears that are hard to get into.
issues.why: Worn synchronizers in the manual gearbox can no longer match gear speeds smoothly. Clutch problems can cause similar grinding.
issues.next: Have the clutch adjustment and fluid checked first. If the synchros are worn, the transmission needs a rebuild or replacement.

issues.sym: Harsh, late or slipping shifts, or the transmission hesitating to go into gear.
issues.why: Owners report shifting faults on early Cobalts that range from shifter cable problems to internal transmission wear.
issues.next: Have the fluid level and trouble codes checked. Rule out the shifter cable before agreeing to major transmission work.

issues.t: Doors lock and unlock by themselves
issues.sym: The power locks cycle on their own, whether the car is running or parked.
issues.why: Owners trace this to failing door lock actuators or electrical faults in the locking system.
issues.next: Note which door makes the noise. A shop can test the lock actuators and the body control module before replacing parts.

issues.sym: Coolant drips or crusty residue at the front of the engine, a falling coolant level, or the temperature gauge rising.
issues.why: The water pump seal on the 2.2L Ecotec wears with age and mileage and starts to leak.
issues.next: Top up with the right coolant and have the leak pressure-tested. Replace the pump before the engine overheats.

issues.t: Shifter may show Park when not in Park (recall)
issues.sym: The shifter reads Park, but the car can roll because the transmission isn't actually in Park.
issues.why: A clip on the shift cable may not have been fully seated. GM recall 09V-073 inspects and secures it.
issues.next: Always set the parking brake. Check your VIN for open recall 09V-073.

issues.t: Weak head protection near the roof (recall)
issues.sym: No symptom. Cars without the optional roof-mounted side airbags may give too little head protection in a crash.
issues.why: Some cars without curtain airbags didn't meet the federal rule for head impact protection on the upper interior. GM recall 07V-014 adds padding.
issues.next: Check your VIN for open recall 07V-014.

issues.t: Headlight shields can come loose and cause glare (recall)
issues.sym: Headlights look odd and oncoming drivers may flash you because of glare.
issues.why: Bulb shields inside the headlamps can loosen from vibration. GM recall 04V-560 fixes the headlamps.
issues.next: Check your VIN for open recall 04V-560.

issues.t: Driver curtain airbag wiring can short (recall)
issues.sym: The airbag warning light may come on. The driver-side curtain airbag might not deploy in a side crash.
issues.why: A misrouted wiring harness for the side-impact sensor can get damaged and short. GM recall 15V-500 reroutes and repairs it.
issues.next: Check your VIN for open recall 15V-500 and get the airbag light checked.

issues.t: Aftermarket ignition switch can slip out of Run (recall)
issues.sym: On a car that had its ignition switch replaced with an aftermarket part, the engine can shut off while driving.
issues.why: Some replacement ignition switches sold in auto parts stores have the same weak design as the original GM switch. Equipment recall 14E-021 covers them.
issues.next: If your switch was ever replaced at an independent shop, ask what part was used and have the GM recall work done to install a correct switch.

issues.sym: The steering suddenly feels stuck or extremely stiff while driving, then may return to normal.
issues.why: Owners link this to the electric power steering motor and its sensor failing, the same part covered by GM's power steering recall.
issues.next: Slow down and steer firmly to a safe stop. Have the power steering system and recall status checked before driving further.
